title: Twenty-one Years and One Locked Corridor
subtitle: 机构与部门 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 机构与部门（社会服务与人际沟通·组织机构）
meta: 主题语境：机构与部门（社会服务与人际沟通·组织机构）　|　核心词汇：department　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 department 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 the director ① opened a department that no board in the city would have funded, and he said the opening was the whole of the year. The ② department, meaning the section and not the building, ran twenty-one years and stayed unstaffed on the plan; a department, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unmanned.

Every ③ department in that office had the same locked corridor at the end of it, and the ④ department at the end, meaning the one they kept for the archive and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever inspected twice. A department, his secretary said, is nine parts paper and one part somebody willing to open; the director said the opening is the part that fills twenty-one years.

The auditor meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the department was the whole of the budget, meaning the division and not the section. The ⑥ department, meaning the division and not any of that, is the only thing in a budget that everybody votes for and nobody visits; department, she said, is either something you open or the only word that means both a section and a division. She said the division is the part they remember.

By 1959 the ⑦ department had become a line in a chart, and the chart had become an argument about the locked corridor. The ⑧ department of the whole thing, the director wrote in September, was one office and twenty-one years of opening; department, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to staff. She said the staffing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ department I remember is the one at the end, which was closed in 1977 and is still described as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ department, the secretary said in 1979, is the only thing that improves by being staffed; every department, she said, is a division that has agreed to look like a section. She said the division was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 部门；处室（指机关里设立的那一处）
B. n. 部门（指那个处室本身，与那栋楼相对）
C. 固定搭配：open a department 开设一个部门
D. n. 部门（指留给档案用的那一处）
E. n. 部门；处（抽象总称，指一间机关里的全部设置）
F. n. 部门（指架构图上写到、被列明的那一处）
G. n. 部门；分部（指预算里被投票的那个单位）
H. n. 分部（抽象总称，指人人投票却无人到访的那个）

items.q: opened a department that no board in the city would have funded
The department, meaning the section and not the building
the department was the whole of the budget
the department had become a line in a chart
The department of the whole thing
A department, the secretary said in 1979

answers.why: open a department 意为“开设一个部门”，1951 年主任开设了一个全城没有一处董事会肯出资的部门。
department 意为“部门”，指那个处室本身而不是那栋楼，它在规划里搁了二十一年而没有人员。
department 意为“部门”，指那间机关里每一处部门，每一处末尾都有同一条锁着的走廊。
department 意为“部门”，指留给档案用的那一处，是唯一有人视察过两次的。
department 意为“部门、分部”，指预算里被投票的那个单位，审计员说这个单位就是那份预算的全部。
department 意为“分部”，指人人投票却无人到访的那个而不是那个处室本身，是预算里人人都投票、却无人去过的东西。
department 意为“部门”，指架构图上写到、被列明的那一处，到 1959 年这个部门成了架构图上的一行。
department 意为“部门、处”，主任九月写道，整件事的部门设置是一间机关和二十一年的开设。
department 意为“部门”，我记得的是末尾那一处，1977 年关闭，至今仍被说成机关里最安静的一处。
department 为抽象总称，秘书 1979 年说，一个部门是唯一会因为配齐人手而变得更好的东西。
